mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 0.5% month-over-month signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.2 percentage points month-over-month indicates a tightening labor market, which is a sign of economic strength and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If UNRATE decreases by more than 0.2pp MoM and S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 5% month-over-month signals increased demand in the housing market, which is a leading indicator of economic growth and leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If HOUST increases by more than 5% MoM and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals increased economic activity, which leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO shows a sustained increase for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 5% and the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.3% month-over-month, the combination signals a tightening monetary policy and inflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tightening monetary policy with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS is above 5% and CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.3% MoM, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.1 percentage points month-over-month, the combination signals a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200k and UNRATE decreases > 0.1pp MoM
failure_condition: If PAYEMS increases by more than 200k and UNRATE decreases by more than 0.1pp MoM, but S&P 500 forward 20-day returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month signals a weakening consumer demand, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS decreases by more than 1% MoM and S&P 500 forward 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decrease in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months signals a contraction in economic activity, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO shows a sustained decrease for three consecutive months and S&P 500 forward 60-day returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances, the hypothesis is rejected.
